name: YASKAWA Electric Corporation
fiscal_year_note: Fiscal year ends end-February. Company label FY2026 = Mar 1, 2026 to Feb 28, 2027 (some data sites call it FY2027, e.g. 'Q2 2027'). Q2 FY2026 (Jun-Aug 2026) was released Oct 9, 2026 after the close; Oct 12 was a Japanese holiday, so the first reaction was Oct 13. Q3 (Sep-Nov) is normally reported in early January. IFRS reporter.
full_year_guidance: FY2026 (Mar 2026-Feb 2027), revised Oct 9, 2026: revenue JPY 600.0bn (prior 580.0; +10.7% YoY), operating profit JPY 57.5bn (cut from 60.0; +21.5% YoY; 9.6% margin), profit before tax JPY 65.5bn, net profit JPY 47.5bn (prior 47.0; analyst average was 45.1), EPS JPY 183.11, DPS JPY 72 (interim 36). Segment OP: Motion Control 39.4 (prior 42.0), Robotics 17.8 (prior 21.0), System Engineering 5.6 (prior 3.2). Revenue raised on a weaker yen; OP cut mainly because the new ERP system hurt 1H production and shipments. FX assumption for Sep 2026-Feb 2027: JPY 155/USD, 180/EUR, 22.0/CNY, 0.107/KRW (April plan: 145/USD, 170/EUR, 20.5/CNY). Implied 2H: revenue JPY 314.4bn, OP JPY 35.4bn (11.3% margin) vs 1H 22.1bn (7.7%) (derived).
fx_sensitivity: Company discloses the impact of a 1% yen move on FY2026 full-year results by currency, but the table text came through garbled. Revenue impact per 1% (fairly clear, Oct 2026 deck): USD about JPY 1.63bn, EUR 0.71bn, CNY 1.35bn, KRW 0.37bn. Operating profit per 1% (low-confidence reading): USD about JPY 0.40bn, EUR about 0.18bn, KRW about 0.09bn, CNY likely about 0.4bn; roughly JPY 1bn of OP for a 1% broad yen move. That is about JPY 0.26bn of annual OP per JPY 1 vs USD. Yen weakness alone lifted the revenue guide by JPY 20bn in October.

physical_ai_exposure.description: Robotics segment (MOTOMAN industrial robots, semiconductor wafer-transfer robots) was 41.5% of 1H FY2026 revenue (45.6% of FY2025). Motion Control servos also sell into robots and semiconductor equipment. Physical AI: MOTOMAN NEXT autonomous AI robot used for physical AI validation with partners (e.g. a strawberry sorting/packing project in 2H); 'Dash 35' plan targets new markets for physical AI. Humanoids: acquired 100% of Tokyo Robotics Inc., developing humanoid-robot actuators, and plans data accumulation and robot design toward commercializing humanoids. Robot Factory No. 5 began full operation integrating servo and robot production.
physical_ai_exposure.optionality_notes: The stock roughly doubled from the March 2026 low (JPY 3,987) to a record JPY 7,915 on Jun 22, 2026 on AI, semiconductor and physical-AI enthusiasm, then fell about 50% to JPY 3,980 after ERP-driven profit misses, a Goldman Sachs downgrade and the October AI-hardware sell-off, even though orders keep setting records. Humanoid work is still pre-commercial, so the market is pricing near-term execution rather than humanoid optionality.

cost_and_supply_chain_notes: Components for 2H production are secured; semiconductors are a bigger concern for FY2027. Labor availability, especially in Japan, is the main production constraint. Rare earths are monitored; long-term magnet supply is secured and rare-earth-free motor technology is in development. Management expects price pass-through to offset about 70% of material cost increases. Capacity: Motion Control capacity to rise 30-40% in 2H vs 1H with two-shift operation; semiconductor-robot capacity needs about 2.7x the 1H level (about 2x now). Footprint mentioned in materials: Japan (Robot Factory No. 5), China (could move to three shifts), Slovenia (European robot plant and logistics hub), Vietnam (PCB supply for drives). ERP (SAP S/4HANA) go-live in May 2026 disrupted output: about JPY 2.5bn OP lost in 1Q, about JPY 10bn of 2Q revenue opportunity lost, about JPY 4bn 1H OP hit; normalization expected in 3Q. US: the April 2026 Q&A says North American Drives margins could approach China's high levels if capital investment at the Franklin campus (Franklin, Wisconsin) proceeds as planned. Tariffs: no yen impact disclosed; the FY2026 plan embeds cost-increase assumptions for geopolitics, transport and petroleum-derived parts (about JPY 4bn of annual risk factors per the 1Q Q&A), and possible additional US tariffs on robots are said to be reflected in the plan. In Oct 2025 management expected no significant cost hit from steel/aluminum tariffs and planned to pass costs through; automakers' worries about Mexico/Canada tariffs held back US-bound auto robot orders.
competition_notes: Management said in Oct 2025 it would take all necessary measures against local Chinese AC servo competitors, and in Apr 2026 that price-led expansion by local manufacturers is approaching its limits; it also restructured Motion Control in China (about JPY 0.4bn) and is exiting about JPY 20bn of low-margin Robotics projects. In China's general servo market Inovance is #1 with about 35% share (H1 2026, up from about 31% in 2025), squeezing Japanese suppliers including Yaskawa; domestic brands hold about 54% of China's industrial robot market (2025, MIR). Yaskawa is pushing its Sigma-Mx servo in China and its China orders rose 35% YoY in Q2 (fifth straight quarter of growth). Management says price revisions are becoming common across the FA industry.
key_drivers: Record orders: Q2 FY2026 JPY 185.4bn (+38% YoY, +13% QoQ); fifth straight quarter of YoY growth
Motion Control orders JPY 91.1bn (+56%); Robotics JPY 77.6bn (+33%)
By region in Q2: Americas JPY 48.8bn (+60%), Other Asia 29.6bn (+53%), Europe 20.9bn (+36%), China 37.5bn (+35%), Japan 48.6bn (+18%)
AI, semiconductor and data-center demand: 1Q semiconductor-related AC servo orders +200% YoY and semiconductor robot orders +141%; U1000 matrix converter orders for US data-center cooling
ERP recovery: implied 2H OP JPY 35.4bn vs 1H 22.1bn; Robotics 2H margin target 9% vs 5.0% in 1H
Management expects order levels to hold through 3Q and 4Q
key_risks: Execution: ERP problems already forced an OP guidance cut (JPY 60.0bn to 57.5bn)
Robotics profitability: 1H segment margin 5.0% (OP -43%); European restructuring costs in Germany
Book-to-bill well above 1 means delivery risk if capacity, labor or chips fall short
Chinese competition in servos and robots (Inovance and other domestic brands)
Yen appreciation after BOJ hikes to 1.25%
AI-capex sentiment: -9.3% on Oct 15; Goldman Sachs downgrade to Neutral; stock about -50% from June high
Net debt position (about JPY 55bn) unlike cash-rich Fanuc

recent_events.event: US reciprocal-tariff announcement triggers a global equity sell-off.
recent_events.stock_reaction: April 2025: -19.1% m/m (3,730 to 3,017); intraday low JPY 2,582

recent_events.event: Q2 FY2025 (Jun-Aug 2025) results after the close: orders turned up (+6% YoY), full-year revenue forecast raised by JPY 10bn, Motion Control margin guided back to 11%, strong AI-related semiconductor demand.
recent_events.stock_reaction: Oct 6: +19.3% (3,178 to 3,790); October 2025 +34.5% m/m (part of the move may be market-wide)

recent_events.event: Q3 FY2025 (Sep-Nov 2025) results: orders +15% YoY (second straight quarter of growth) while profits were still declining (FY2025 OP ended -5.7%).
Broad Japanese equity sell-off through March 2026.

FY2025 results (revenue JPY 542.1bn, OP 47.3bn); 4Q orders +20% YoY (Motion Control +47%); FY2026 guidance OP JPY 60.0bn (+26.8%) at JPY 145/USD; Tokyo Robotics acquisition and humanoid actuator development disclosed.
Record intraday high JPY 7,915 (about +98% from the March 2026 low of JPY 3,987).

Q1 FY2026 (Mar-May 2026): record AC servo and robot orders (total +29%) but OP -19.2% to JPY 8.5bn after the S/4HANA ERP go-live disrupted production (about JPY 2.5bn OP lost) plus JPY 1.0bn European restructuring; guidance kept.

Q2 FY2026 results after close: record orders JPY 185.4bn (+38%); revenue forecast raised to JPY 600bn on the weak yen; OP forecast cut to JPY 57.5bn (ERP); NI raised to JPY 47.5bn vs JPY 45.1bn consensus.
recent_events.stock_reaction: Oct 13 (next session): opened +3.0%, high +4.9%, closed +1.2% at 4,840 on 11.7m shares (about 3x normal)

recent_events.event: Goldman Sachs downgrades Yaskawa to Neutral from Buy (date approximate; GS had removed it from its APAC Conviction List about two months earlier).
recent_events.stock_reaction: Slide continued to a 2026 low of JPY 3,775 intraday on Oct 23 (-13.8% vs Oct 16 close)

recent_events.event: Websites restored after a suspension over a PHP vulnerability; company found no unauthorized access or data leakage.

notes: Price is the Oct 26, 2026 close; shares exclude 7.25m treasury shares (Aug 31, 2026); USD conversion at JPY 156.91/USD. Q2 standalone revenue (146.6), OP (13.6) and net income (13.6) are derived as 1H minus 1Q; the 1Q-to-2Q OP bridge (+5.1) supports the OP figure. Regional Q2 order amounts come from TechNews and sum to the company total of JPY 185.4bn. cash_and_investments = cash 66.1 + current other financial assets 4.1; non-current other financial assets of JPY 93.6bn (mostly investment securities) excluded. total_debt = bonds and borrowings 109.3 + lease liabilities 16.0. Geo and segment mixes are 1H FY2026 revenue (FY2025 geo: Japan 27.4, Americas 23.7, China 21.4, Other Asia 14.9, Europe 12.6). FY2025 R&D (21.1) and FY2026 D&A plan (24.0) are read from a hard-to-read chart; medium confidence. FCF = operating CF 52.2 less capex 46.2. Valuation computed by us at JPY 3,980: P/E on company EPS 183.11 (Yahoo Japan 21.96x at 4,022), P/B on owners' equity 504.1, EV/EBITDA = (market cap + debt - cash + NCI 10.5) / (OP 57.5 + D&A 24.0). FX OP sensitivities are a low-confidence reading of a garbled table. US Wisconsin plant: the company's Apr 2026 Q&A confirms ongoing capital investment at its Franklin campus (Franklin is in Wisconsin), tied to North American Drives margins; the size of the investment and any robot-production scope (background recollection: about USD 180m announced in 2025) were not verified this session. Goldman Sachs action dates are approximate (from relative dates on stockanalysis).
